title: Modiolaria bourailensis T.D.A. Cockerell, 1929 is a New Caledonia endemic Arcuatula (Bivalvia: Mytilidae)
content: In 1928, Thomas Cockerell visited New Caledonia and collected molluscs on the West coast, leading to the description of several land and freshwater snails (Cockerell, 1929a, 1930a, b, c) and to a general paper on the freshwater fauna of the island (Cockerell, 1929b). On the way between Nouméa and Muéo, his end point to the North, he collected “river drift at the sea coast a few miles from Bourail” from which he described Modiolaria bourailensis (Fig. 1A), and from which Solem (1960) catalogued the land snails, and Haase & Bouchet (1998) described Leiorhagium solemi (Gastropoda: Tateidae). Modiolaria bourailensis has remained an elusive species, treated only once in the literature: Starmühlner (1970) recorded it from several estuaries on both the West and East coasts of New Caledonia, and transferred it—without comment—to the genus Modiolus, where it remains today (MolluscaBase eds, 2025a). Huber (2010) did not mention the species in his Compendium of Bivalves. We have collected M. bourailensis at the type locality, and the purpose of this research note is to record its life habit and discuss its systematic position based on molecular data.
